important_confusion_boundaries: A material contour belongs to the liquid/paste/gel body itself, not vessel walls, outlet construction, garment seams, hair or anatomical body silhouette.
A liquid coil remains a continuous material thread; a coil-built clay vessel concerns assembled wall structure.
A free body outline is different from local surface wetness, gloss, printed decoration or a light projection.
Detached particles or droplets and liquid bubbles do not substitute for one connected narrowed or beaded material body.
Flame material contour is separate from the pattern of light cast onto a receiving surface. Existing flame candidates should be reused only with their full bundled source effects.
Still appearance cannot establish viscosity values, elasticity, phase chemistry, stress magnitude, temperature, flow duration, future breakage or production history.

The additions describe complete optional configurations and declare the additional subject/material/relationship effects; discovering them does not authorize introducing owners into a frozen still life.
recommendations: Add specific positive contours rather than synonyms of shape, liquid or honey.
Use the same original query for before/after evaluation; do not add spoon/jar strings to generic form candidates to win the known probe.
Compare exposure of existing jet/rivulet/droplet forms as well as the six new families; report complete source conditions/effects when discussing fit.
Keep all additions discovery-only until source-native meaning review. Any appearance-only request must reject source effects outside open subject/material/relationship scopes.
Retain the richer existing crown splash, meniscus and clay-action records rather than creating near-duplicates.

research_sources.title: APS DFD — Sagging(s) of Viscous Filaments
research_sources.supports: Researcher-authored explanation distinguishes a smoothly sagging liquid filament from a U-shaped filament with a thinner middle and thicker sides. The same account describes buckled loops. These are spatial forms of the material, not the shape of its support.

research_sources.title: Dynamics of liquid rope coiling
research_sources.supports: Experimental and numerical work studies the coils of a viscous liquid thread falling onto a solid surface, including coil and thread radii and buckling of a piled column. This supports a connected deposited coil, not arbitrary motion of a rigid rope.

research_sources.title: Study on stretching liquid bridges with symmetric and asymmetric surface wettability
research_sources.supports: Liquid bridges between separating plates can thin and break; wetting and stretching conditions alter where separation occurs. A continuous narrowed bridge is a particular pre-breakup configuration, not a guarantee for all liquids.

research_sources.title: Pearling Instabilities of a Viscoelastic Thread
research_sources.supports: The experiments distinguish beaded filament morphology from a different blistering instability in stretched polymer solutions. A visible connected beaded form is distinct from detached spray and does not identify the chemistry from pixels.

research_sources.title: Solid Drops: Large Capillary Deformations of Immersed Elastic Rods
research_sources.supports: Experiments on soft centimeter-scale gel specimens show surface-stress deformation, including rounding of prism edges, shortening and widening of cylinders, and bending of a slender triangular specimen. This supports deformable non-anatomical masses at photographic scale; it does not identify modulus or force from appearance.

research_sources.title: MIT engineers introduce the Oreometer
research_sources.supports: MIT describes frosting and cookie cream among materials that remain soft solids without sufficient applied stress and flow when stressed. A particular peak or ridge is an authored illustration rather than an experimentally universal contour.

research_sources.title: MIT Mechanical Engineering — How slippery surfaces allow sticky pastes and gels to slide
research_sources.supports: Institutional account explains yield-stress gels and pastes, with examples in food and cosmetics, and distinguishes intact plug-like shape from sheared material. The statement supports a coherent paste mass, not exact rheological measurement from a still image.

authored_additions.why_new: Adds a positive bend and continuous body contour. Existing continuous transfer/jet candidates specify a path or event without this macroscopic bent form; the conceptual anti-gravity liquid record has no determinate contour.
Adds a looped deposited liquid body. Clay coils joined into vessel walls describe construction; water columns do not describe loops or piled volume.
Adds a constricted bounded liquid volume and flared end regions. The meniscus candidate concerns a local vessel-wall edge; transfer and droplet records lack the two-ended necked geometry.
Adds alternating broad lobes and narrow continuous links. Surface droplets, airborne spray and bubbles are distinct existing meanings without a single continuous outer material body.

Adds the volumetric contour of a non-anatomical soft mass. Existing gelatinous animal bodies are anatomical; clay vessel assembly and general dough-surface texture do not state these bounded rounded shoulders.

Adds a whole soft-material mound, tapered crest and connected folded ridge. The clay-lump record binds finger contact, local grooves and an adjoining edge; it does not state this global mound volume and would add a hand action if substituted.
